summary: LSU’s next step is cleaner protection and disciplined coverage against Louisiana Tech. Watch whether the guards hold the pocket without a quarterback escape, and whether the defense can force long drives instead of trading big plays.

items.headline: SEC meeting ends with discussions continuing
items.tldr: WBRZ reports that expulsion was off Thursday’s agenda and LSU left Wright and Harris off its roster. The roster decision does not mean the wider conference dispute is resolved.

items.headline: Kiffin wants better guard play despite a sack-free opener
items.tldr: Watch whether Leavitt can complete the play from the pocket. An escape that saves a possession is useful, but it can hide a blocking problem.

items.headline: Kiffin expects more opportunities for Elzy
items.tldr: Watch his involvement without treating a bigger role as guaranteed. The useful signal is whether the next target produces a routine completion and keeps the offense moving.

items.headline: Ross scored on an interception and added a sack against Clemson
items.tldr: Watch whether LSU can disrupt the next opponent without needing another defensive touchdown. Pressure and sound tackling are the more repeatable ways to end a drive.

items.headline: Friday’s game guide sets LSU–Tech kickoff at 6:32 p.m. CT
items.tldr: The guide lists SEC Network+ and a sold-out Tiger Stadium. Set up your stream early, and use the parking and traffic links before heading to campus.

lead.headline: Give Leavitt a cleaner pocket.
lead.body: Watch the guards before judging the passing game. Clean protection would let LSU finish plays without asking its quarterback to rescue them.

matchup.question: What should LSU improve against Louisiana Tech?
matchup.answer: Keep the pocket intact and make the routine completion. On defense, stay disciplined against the deep ball and force the opponent to build a drive.

signals.title: Guard play
signals.detail: Watch whether the guards hold their assignments when the quarterback stays in place. Escaping pressure should be an option, not the whole protection plan.
signals.prompt: What should I watch up front for LSU?

signals.title: Coverage discipline
signals.detail: Watch the first deep route and how the safety responds. Keeping the ball in front can make the opponent earn another set of downs.
signals.prompt: What should LSU watch in Louisiana Tech’s passing game?

signals.title: Receiver involvement
signals.detail: Watch which receiver becomes the reliable option when the first read is covered. A larger role has to show up in useful plays, not just snaps.
signals.prompt: What should I watch from Malik Elzy?

signals.title: Defensive disruption
signals.detail: Watch whether the defense turns pressure into a stop without losing its tackling shape. A takeaway touchdown is a bonus, not a requirement.
signals.prompt: What should LSU’s defense carry into this game?
